also: speak of the devil and he appears

terms.gloss: speak of the devil (here he comes)
terms.grammar: fixed phrase, said when someone arrives just as he is being talked about
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.33.4: dē Varrōne loquēbāmur: lupus in fābulā: vēnit enim ad mē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “the wolf in the story”: Latin names a wolf where English names the devil.

evidence: Plaut. Stich. 577: atque eccum tibi lupum in sermōne

phrases.latin: Hem tibi autem. — Quidnam est? — Lupus in fābulā. — Pater est? — Ipsus est.
phrases.english: Look out! — What is it? — Speak of the devil. — Is it Dad? — It’s him.

phrases.latin: atque eccum tibi lupum in sermōne: praesēns ēsuriēns adest.
phrases.english: and speak of the devil: here he is in person, hungry.
